sentence: She avoided ___ by the visitors.
setupText: The photographer stayed behind the screen so that visitors would not see her. Preserve who sees whom.
taskText: She avoided ___ by the visitors.
text: The photographer stayed behind the screen so that visitors would not see her. Preserve who sees whom. She avoided ___ by the visitors.
explanation: Avoid takes an -ing form; being seen makes her the person receiving the visitors' attention.

rationales.seeing: Seeing makes her the observer, whereas the visitors would see her.
rationales.being seen: Avoid takes an -ing form; being seen makes her the person receiving the visitors' attention.
rationales.to be seen: The passive meaning fits, but avoid needs being seen rather than to be seen.
rationales.having seen: Having seen makes her the person who had observed something, reversing the roles.

sentence: 'Reviewers consider this camera reliable.' This camera is considered ___.
setupText: Rewrite the judgment with the camera as subject, preserving the present assessment.
taskText: 'Reviewers consider this camera reliable.' This camera is considered ___.
text: Rewrite the judgment with the camera as subject, preserving the present assessment. 'Reviewers consider this camera reliable.' This camera is considered ___.
explanation: Is considered to be reports an assessment of the subject; this differs from consider doing an action.

rationales.being reliable: Passive considered uses to be here, not an -ing clause naming an option under consideration.
rationales.to have been reliable: The perfect phrase places the reliability earlier instead of preserving the present assessment.
rationales.to be reliable: Is considered to be reports an assessment of the subject; this differs from consider doing an action.
rationales.reliably: Reliably describes how something acts; the judgment is that the camera itself is reliable.

sentence: The builder expects ___ the roof by the time the inspector arrives.
setupText: Use the perfect infinitive to make completion before the inspection explicit.
taskText: The builder expects ___ the roof by the time the inspector arrives.
text: Use the perfect infinitive to make completion before the inspection explicit. The builder expects ___ the roof by the time the inspector arrives.
explanation: To have + past participle presents repair as complete before the inspection time.

rationales.to have repaired: To have + past participle presents repair as complete before the inspection time.
rationales.to having repaired: After infinitival to, use have rather than having.
rationales.having repaired: Expect does not directly take this -ing clause for the expected action.
rationales.to have repairing: Have needs repaired, not repairing, in the perfect infinitive.

sentence: The panel postponed ___ whom ___ until all applications were in.
setupText: Choose the pair that completes both linked verb patterns correctly.
taskText: The panel postponed ___ whom ___ until all applications were in.
text: Choose the pair that completes both linked verb patterns correctly. The panel postponed ___ whom ___ until all applications were in.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1504:An infinitival question within a gerund complement
explanation: Postpone takes an -ing activity; decide can be followed by a question-word phrase with a to-infinitive.

rationales.deciding / interviewing: Deciding fits postponed, but the embedded choice uses whom to interview, not whom interviewing.
rationales.to decide / interviewing: Postpone needs deciding, and the embedded question needs whom to interview.
rationales.to decide / to interview: To interview fits after whom, but postpone takes deciding rather than to decide.
rationales.deciding / to interview: Postpone takes an -ing activity; decide can be followed by a question-word phrase with a to-infinitive.

sentence: 'The team decided that it would not publish the survey yet.'
setupText: Choose the rewrite that says the team made a decision against publication.
taskText: 'The team decided that it would not publish the survey yet.'
text: Choose the rewrite that says the team made a decision against publication. 'The team decided that it would not publish the survey yet.'
options: The team decided not to publish the survey yet.
The team did not decide to publish the survey yet.
The team decided publishing the survey not yet.
The team decided to publish the survey yet.
answer: The team decided not to publish the survey yet.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1505:Negation of a decision versus a decision not to act
explanation: Not belongs to the infinitive, so the decision is specifically to withhold publication.

rationales.The team did not decide to publish the s: This says no positive publication decision was made; it need not mean a decision against publication was made.
rationales.The team decided not to publish the surv: Not belongs to the infinitive, so the decision is specifically to withhold publication.
rationales.The team decided publishing the survey n: This is not the required decide-plus-infinitive pattern, and not yet is misplaced.
rationales.The team decided to publish the survey y: This removes the decision against publication and leaves yet without the intended negative context.

sentence: 'I tried to open the jammed drawer for ten minutes, but eventually called a carpenter.'
setupText: Read the complete account. Choose the conclusion it supports.
taskText: 'I tried to open the jammed drawer for ten minutes, but eventually called a carpenter.'
text: Read the complete account. Choose the conclusion it supports. 'I tried to open the jammed drawer for ten minutes, but eventually called a carpenter.'
options: The speaker opened it by experimenting with a new technique.
The speaker avoided attempting to open it until help arrived.
The speaker remembers opening it before it became jammed.
The speaker attempted to open it; the account does not report success.
answer: The speaker attempted to open it; the account does not report success.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1506:Try to as an attempt without an entailment of success
explanation: Try to + verb expresses an effort toward an action; it does not itself assert achievement.

rationales.The speaker opened it by experimenting w: The account supplies neither a successful opening nor a newly tested method.
rationales.The speaker avoided attempting to open i: Tried to open explicitly states that an attempt was made.
rationales.The speaker attempted to open it; the ac: Try to + verb expresses an effort toward an action; it does not itself assert achievement.
rationales.The speaker remembers opening it before: This is an attempt at the jammed drawer, not recollection of an earlier opening.

sentence: I remember ___ not to unplug the device during the update.
setupText: The technician gave the speaker a warning last week. Complete the speaker's memory of receiving that warning.
taskText: I remember ___ not to unplug the device during the update.
text: The technician gave the speaker a warning last week. Complete the speaker's memory of receiving that warning. I remember ___ not to unplug the device during the update.
explanation: Remember being told recalls receiving someone else's instruction.

rationales.being told: Remember being told recalls receiving someone else's instruction.
rationales.telling: Telling would make the speaker give the warning rather than receive it.
rationales.to tell: Remember to tell describes a pending duty to give a warning, not a memory of receiving one.
rationales.to be told: This does not express recollection of an earlier experience; that requires the passive -ing form.

sentence: We regret ___ you that the venue is unavailable on your chosen date.
setupText: Choose the phrase that conventionally introduces unwelcome news in this formal letter.
taskText: We regret ___ you that the venue is unavailable on your chosen date.
text: Choose the phrase that conventionally introduces unwelcome news in this formal letter. We regret ___ you that the venue is unavailable on your chosen date.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1508:Regret to inform as a current speech act
explanation: Regret to inform conventionally expresses regret while delivering unwelcome information.

rationales.informing: Regret informing normally looks back unhappily on having informed someone, rather than introducing the news now.
rationales.inform: Regret does not take the basic verb inform directly in this formula.
rationales.to informing: This formula needs the basic verb after to.
rationales.to inform: Regret to inform conventionally expresses regret while delivering unwelcome information.

sentence: She then went on ___ staffing needs.
setupText: The lecturer finished discussing costs and introduced staffing as the next subject. Preserve that sequence.
taskText: She then went on ___ staffing needs.
text: The lecturer finished discussing costs and introduced staffing as the next subject. Preserve that sequence. She then went on ___ staffing needs.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1509:Go on to do as a subsequent action
explanation: Go on to + verb introduces a subsequent action or stage after an earlier one.

rationales.discussing: Went on discussing would mean continuing the same discussion, not moving to the new subject specified.
rationales.to discuss: Go on to + verb introduces a subsequent action or stage after an earlier one.
rationales.discuss: The basic verb cannot directly follow went on in this construction.
rationales.to discussing: To discussing does not form either the continuing or subsequent-action pattern.

sentence: 'Taking this post means working some weekends.'
setupText: The rota now includes Saturdays. Choose the meaning of the speaker's comment.
taskText: 'Taking this post means working some weekends.'
text: The rota now includes Saturdays. Choose the meaning of the speaker's comment. 'Taking this post means working some weekends.'
options: The speaker intends to accept the post on a weekend.
Weekend work is something the speaker remembers doing in an earlier post.
The speaker tried weekend work to decide whether to accept the post.
Weekend work is part of what accepting the post involves.
answer: Weekend work is part of what accepting the post involves.
explanation: Mean + -ing expresses what a situation involves or entails.

rationales.The speaker intends to accept the post o: Means working expresses a consequence, not the intention conveyed by mean to.
rationales.Weekend work is something the speaker re: The statement describes what the new post involves, not a remembered previous job.
rationales.Weekend work is part of what accepting t: Mean + -ing expresses what a situation involves or entails.
rationales.The speaker tried weekend work to decide: No experiment is described; the sentence links acceptance with its consequence.

sentence: Put the roof first.
setupText: Someone needs to repair the roof. Choose the sentence that preserves that meaning.
taskText: Put the roof first.
text: Someone needs to repair the roof. Choose the sentence that preserves that meaning. Put the roof first.
options: The roof needs to be repair.
explanation: Need + -ing can have passive meaning: the roof needs someone to repair it.

Need + -ing can have passive meaning: the roof needs someone to repair it.
This makes the roof the performer of repair rather than the thing needing repair.
After infinitival to, use a basic verb; this combination is malformed.
The passive infinitive needs the past participle repaired after to be, not repair.

sentence: With such a small storage room, we cannot afford ___ every old display.
setupText: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar.
taskText: With such a small storage room, we cannot afford ___ every old display.
text: Complete the sentence with the correct grammar. With such a small storage room, we cannot afford ___ every old display.
explanation: Afford to + verb can concern practical resources, including space, as well as money.

rationales.kept: The past form kept cannot directly follow afford; use to keep.
rationales.keep: The infinitive after afford requires to.
rationales.to keeping: After this to, the verb must be the basic form keep.
rationales.to keep: Afford to + verb can concern practical resources, including space, as well as money.

sentence: The witness saw the woman ___ the bridge.
setupText: A witness watched from the woman's first step onto the bridge until she reached the other bank. Choose the wording that presents the crossing as a whole event.
taskText: The witness saw the woman ___ the bridge.
text: A witness watched from the woman's first step onto the bridge until she reached the other bank. Choose the wording that presents the crossing as a whole event. The witness saw the woman ___ the bridge.
explanation: See + object + basic verb can present the observed action as a whole event.

rationales.to cross: Active see + object does not take a to-infinitive in this direct perception pattern.
rationales.cross: See + object + basic verb can present the observed action as a whole event.
rationales.crossing: Crossing presents the action in progress; it does not foreground the whole crossing as requested.
rationales.crossed: Crossed cannot serve as the action complement after saw the woman here.

sentence: 'The supervisor made us repeat the measurements.' We were made ___ the measurements.
setupText: Rewrite the sentence in the passive while preserving the enforced action.
taskText: 'The supervisor made us repeat the measurements.' We were made ___ the measurements.
text: Rewrite the sentence in the passive while preserving the enforced action. 'The supervisor made us repeat the measurements.' We were made ___ the measurements.
explanation: The bare infinitive after active make gains to in the passive: were made to repeat.

rationales.repeat: The active pattern uses repeat without to, but passive were made requires to repeat.
rationales.repeating: This passive causative does not use an -ing complement.
rationales.to repeat: The bare infinitive after active make gains to in the passive: were made to repeat.
rationales.to repeated: Use the basic verb repeat after to, not repeated.

sentence: 'The host let the guests use the kitchen.'
setupText: Put the guests first, preserving permission to use the kitchen in standard written English.
taskText: 'The host let the guests use the kitchen.'
text: Put the guests first, preserving permission to use the kitchen in standard written English. 'The host let the guests use the kitchen.'
options: The guests were let to use the kitchen.
The guests were allowed to use the kitchen.
The guests were made to use the kitchen.
The guests were allowed using the kitchen.
answer: The guests were allowed to use the kitchen.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1515:Preserving let permission in a passive rewrite
explanation: Allowed to supplies the ordinary passive expression for the permission given by let someone do.

rationales.The guests were allowed to use the kitch: Allowed to supplies the ordinary passive expression for the permission given by let someone do.
Let does not form this ordinary passive with to use; use were allowed to use.
Made to changes permission into an enforced action.
rationales.The guests were allowed using the kitche: When the guests are permitted to act, allowed is followed by to use, not using.

sentence: The guide advised ___ early and advised us ___ a map.
setupText: Choose the pair that completes both standard advice patterns.
taskText: The guide advised ___ early and advised us ___ a map.
text: Choose the pair that completes both standard advice patterns. The guide advised ___ early and advised us ___ a map.
focusKey: coverage-gerunds-and-infinitives-b2-1516:Advise doing versus advise someone to do
explanation: Advise can take an -ing activity directly or a person followed by a to-infinitive.

rationales.to leave / carrying: Without a person after advised, use leaving; with us, use to carry.
rationales.leaving / carrying: Leaving fits the first pattern, but advised us needs to carry.
rationales.to leave / to carry: To carry fits advised us, but directly advised to leave lacks the person required by that active pattern.
rationales.leaving / to carry: Advise can take an -ing activity directly or a person followed by a to-infinitive.

sentence: The report is worth ___ carefully before publication.
setupText: The report needs an editor's attention. Complete the sentence with the passive meaning that the report deserves that attention.
taskText: The report is worth ___ carefully before publication.
text: The report needs an editor's attention. Complete the sentence with the passive meaning that the report deserves that attention. The report is worth ___ carefully before publication.
explanation: Being checked supplies a passive -ing form after worth; the report receives the checking.

rationales.to be checked: Worth takes an -ing complement, not a to-infinitive.
rationales.being checked: Being checked supplies a passive -ing form after worth; the report receives the checking.
rationales.having checked: This active perfect form would make the report the checker rather than the checked object.
rationales.to checking: Worth does not take the extra to in this pattern.

sentence: She objected to ___ without her knowledge.
setupText: The visitor did not want staff to record her conversation. Complete her objection, preserving who would do the recording.
taskText: She objected to ___ without her knowledge.
text: The visitor did not want staff to record her conversation. Complete her objection, preserving who would do the recording. She objected to ___ without her knowledge.
explanation: Object to + being + past participle expresses opposition to receiving an action.

rationales.recording: Recording would make her the person producing a recording, not the person recorded.
rationales.to be recorded: The to in object to is a preposition, so it takes being recorded.
rationales.being recorded: Object to + being + past participle expresses opposition to receiving an action.
rationales.have been recorded: After the preposition to, this form would need having, not have.

sentence: The wall appears ___ recently.
setupText: The wall is dry now, but yesterday's photo shows fresh paint. Choose the phrase making the earlier painting explicit.
taskText: The wall appears ___ recently.
text: The wall is dry now, but yesterday's photo shows fresh paint. Choose the phrase making the earlier painting explicit. The wall appears ___ recently.
explanation: The perfect passive infinitive places the painting before the present appearance and makes the wall its receiver.

rationales.to have been painted: The perfect passive infinitive places the painting before the present appearance and makes the wall its receiver.
rationales.to have painted: This active perfect form would make the wall perform the painting.
rationales.to be painting: This makes the wall the painter and presents an action in progress now.
rationales.having been painted: Appear does not take this -ing clause directly as its complement.

sentence: 'It is important that visitors keep their tickets.' It is important ___ their tickets.
setupText: Rewrite the sentence without changing who performs the action.
taskText: 'It is important that visitors keep their tickets.' It is important ___ their tickets.
text: Rewrite the sentence without changing who performs the action. 'It is important that visitors keep their tickets.' It is important ___ their tickets.
explanation: For introduces the subject of the infinitive, making visitors the people who must keep the tickets.

rationales.visitors keeping: This does not supply the standard for-plus-subject infinitive after important in the given frame.
rationales.for visitors keeping: After the subject visitors in this for-clause, use to keep.
rationales.for visitors to keeping: An infinitival to takes keep rather than keeping.
rationales.for visitors to keep: For introduces the subject of the infinitive, making visitors the people who must keep the tickets.
